experiment: M1C.4 — churn-regime scaling & switching audit of the existing canonical Variant A trajectories (deterministic dynamics audit, no new model)
research_question: Why do the single-step rebound/contraction events proven in M1C.3 organize into a long-lived churn regime? Is there cross-K stable macroscopic structure, a simple switching rhythm, and a deterministic approach-to-stop signature?
audit_scope: Existing canonical Variant A only: q_near, alpha=0.25, exact tol=1e-12, T_max=5000, K in {50,100,200,400}, deterministic expected-mass path. No new q/alpha/K/stochasticity/2D; trajectories regenerated deterministically (bit-identical to committed results).

churn_window_definition.onset: first active round t with D_max < onset_below (M1B.2 operational macroscopic-cleanup boundary; documented there as an approximate phase divider)
churn_window_definition.end: last active round t = t_stop - 1 (the stopping state itself is the stop event, not churn)
churn_window_definition.status: analysis convention reusing the existing M1B.2 divider; not a claimed sharp transition (M1B.2: no clear breakpoint exists)

R_t_definition: R_t = max over j with gamma_t(j) > 0 of [ M_t * max(Delta(j), 0) / gamma_t(j) ], where gamma_t(j) = D_max(t) - D_TM_new,t(j) (positive at every prefix on an active step, M1C.2) and Delta(j) = G_near(j) - j/K. Equivalence R_t > 1 iff D_max rebound is exact in real arithmetic (verified per round against the M1C.3 excess criterion). gamma_t(j) > 0 always holds on active steps in exact arithmetic, so no boundary case exists at gamma = 0; the implementation guards fp only.

switch_convention.definition: large boundary switch: |Delta a| > threshold (existing M1A.1 diagnostic threshold; M1A.1 verified such jumps are real peak switches)

recurrence_audit.summary_state: [D_max, a_t, moved_mass, R_t] standardized within the churn window
recurrence_audit.note: stride sampling makes distances upper bounds on full-density near-returns; convention recorded

no_forced_theory: no cycle/invariant-distribution/universal-fraction/attractor/chaos/ergodicity claims; 'metastable churn regime' is descriptive candidate terminology only
